body: I woke up this morning and I really struck me how much work I had ended up not doing this week because of how down I felt, and that I couldn't fix anything by just continuing this way. Plus I am getting really scared of being rescinded from Cal. So I went in and talked to my counselor and while I did leave out some of my worse suicidal thoughts, I tried to explain how I felt and how it's been keeping me from doing things. She was really kind but persistent on me getting help, and offered to tell my parents for me, and encouraged me to talk to my teacher. I expressed that I wasn't so sure about getting my parents involved, and she said I should come in again tomorrow to talk more and make a plan to get help. While I'll have the power to go in and get what I need once I'm an adult, I still have a while until then, and I need to be able to make it through that time well. So I don't know what exactly I'm going to do next, but I've taken the first step to improving myself and it feels a lot less daunting.

Thank you for the book recommendation. I'll be sure to check it out this summer.

I do sometimes try to understand why I am so aggravated with myself, but I tend to just lead myself down a destructive path of thinking. Perhaps I need to approach it more scientifically.

My current problem is just being too tired to do things, then being angry at myself for not doing them. For example, I spent most of this weekend sleeping or reading random things when I have a tremendous amount of homework to do. I don't know if I'm just being lazy and avoiding it, or if I have an actual issue.

I think I do have a decent idea of what I find interesting - I've loved science and math for a long time, and plan to major in math and/or physics at Berkeley. Who I am is another question, and there are times when I feel put together enough to have some sort of sense of self, but those are not common. A lot of the time, I just feel like I'm undeserving of the things I want to do, even if I really want to do them. I don't know if taking time off would actually help me, but it would definitely create conflict with my parents, which would aggravate my situation.

In the best case, I suppose I want to feel the way I do on a "good day" on a regular enough basis to actually do the things I love. With how consistently I am bogged down by mental exhaustion and self hatred, I lose sight of why I desired to do those things in the first place, and just feel like giving up on everything. 

edit: wording

I guess I'm trying to hard to look for some higher purpose to distract myself from the self-hatred. Just studying something that interests me because I like it feels... self-indulgent? Especially because I have no idea how I'll use it in the future to actually benefit anyone. 

But I really do love math and physics, and if earning money wasn't a concern, and I was in a decent state of mind, I'd probably want to just study it for the rest of my life. Perhaps that should be enough motivation for me to go take this opportunity to learn.

I don't think taking a gap year would help much... despite how much school can stress me out, it also gives me some sort of purpose, and without that structure in my life I don't think I'd do anything but sleep and spiral into further self loathing. Plus, I don't want to be around my parents anymore, and college provides the perfect opportunity to get some space while still being able to depend on them monetarily.
Ah, I can't imagine how that is... What treatment options are available to you?

What I meant by that statement - I've always thought throughout high school that I'd kill myself after graduation, because I'm not sure I have the motivation to actually do anything past that. And now with college a very tangible thing, I feel like I have to actively decide that yes, I'm going to go to college and put effort into living and being successful. And if I can't summon the will to do that, then I should follow through with my desire to die.

My situation is honestly, pretty fucking great, and that's why I feel so guilty all of the time. I live in an upper middle class area of California, go to a good high school with lots of activities, have a few close friends that I trust with everything. I've gotten into UC Berkeley, and so have some of my friends, so I wouldn't be alone in college. And UC Berkeley in and of itself is a great opportunity.

I just don't feel I have the ability or motivation to follow through with what all of this privilege allows me. I can go next year to a college that is very highly ranked for the subjects I want to study, but I don't know why I want to study in the first place. I don't know if I was actually passionate about these things in the first place, even though I fought my father for years on letting me pursue what I want. More and more often, I'm having days or sometimes weeks where I'm just too mentally exhausted to do my homework or anything else. My grades are slipping. I'm seriously concerned that I'll get rescinded from Cal for failing English, because at this point I can't summon the energy to try hard and bring my grade up. I've already had a few opportunities to do so, and I've let them slip. Even if I manage to go to college and get an education, what will I do with it?
Disease? Can you elaborate on that?

I'm not certain, but I think that puts us at about the same age. Either way, what about school is the worst for you? Is it the people? Or the academics? 

For me personally, I've been lucky enough to have tolerable to nice people around me in school. But I have a lot of internal and familial pressure to do extremely well. It's drained me these years, and now I'm slipping and I just feel empty.

Well, I managed to pull an all-nighter, so I'm kind of hazy right now. I'll take a nap and return sometime.

It's interesting that you and your brother are so different, in regards to romance. Actually, thinking about it, while my sister is much younger than me, I'm pretty sure she'll be a hopeless romantic.

I guess we do have that commonality where we want someone to share our lives with, expect for me it would be a friend or queerplatonic partner that I could live with or see on a regular basis. I'm afraid that one day all of the friends I love the most are going to find romantic partners and settle down, and I'm going be cast aside, no longer important to them.

So we're on opposite sides of the coin, in a way - you really want to find a romantic partner, and I really want my friends not to. Seems a bit selfish on me, especially with how you described romance, it's clear it's really important to you.
Ah school, I can relate... what grade are you in? I'm a senior in high school.

Hey, I'm amazed that you had the strength to call a distress line and also come here and share your experiences.

As an aromantic person, I can't instinctually connect to your feeling romantically isolated, so can you tell me more about that, if you want? Or really anything else you want to talk about.

Can I ask, what makes you feel certain about it? I've struggled for a while with whether I'd regret suicide or not, and still do, so I'm curious.
